paragraphs: Ozempic, originally developed in 2017 to treat type 2 diabetes, has rapidly transformed into a massive cultural phenomenon due to its weight-loss effects.

Driven by aggressive advertising campaigns that cost over half a billion dollars annually, advertisements for these injections have become completely pervasive in the United States. Media platforms frequently broadcast before and after videos that show larger bodies in purely negative, depressing terms, which further stigmatize weight issues. This exposure creates intense social pressure across all age groups and genders to pursue extreme thinness, reminiscent of the diet culture of the 1990s.

Scientific research warns that this damages body image and drives individuals toward risky behaviors, including disordered eating and illegal online purchases by people who don’t qualify medically. Even peak professional athletes like Serena Williams have become commercial ambassadors for these wellness platforms. Experts warn that marketing is overshadowing scientific caution and the potential side effects of these powerful drugs.

paragraphs: At first, Ozempic helped people with diabetes, but it is now famous all over the world for helping people lose weight.

The companies which make these injections spend hundreds of millions of dollars on television advertisements. Today, almost every adult in the United States sees these ads every week. The advertisements always show thin people who look very happy, which puts a lot of pressure on normal people to change their bodies immediately. This pressure is dangerous because it makes people feel bad about their weight, and some even stop eating healthy food or buy the drug illegally on the internet. Even famous sports stars get to sell these products, for example, Serena Williams.
Scientists say we must be very careful because the media talks about a miracle drug, but people forget about the dangerous medical risks.

paragraphs: Ozempic is now very famous in America. First, it helps sick people, but now many people use it to look thin.

The companies spend a lot of money on big television advertisements. Normal parents and children see these advertisements every week. The videos show that thin people are always happy and big people are sad. This makes everyone want to lose weight. It makes people feel bad about their bodies. Some people even buy the medicine online without a doctor’s prescription.
Scientists say that this is dangerous. We must follow the rules of science, not television. We must speak about the risks of Ozempic, too.
